points.why: It records A−B for each run and treats a crossing of zero as the decision flipping.

It varies each input low/high with the others held at baseline, builds a tornado chart, and reports breakeven values. It uses justified ranges instead of a fixed ±25%, which is the same method in substance.
It names the parameter that can flip the result as the crux and recommends measuring velocity drag first.
It states that one-at-a-time testing misses interactions and that the inputs are likely correlated, so they could be wrong together.
